title: S switches timeline snapping off and on
goal: Clips snap to the playhead, cuts and each other while you drag them, which is right most of the time, but there is no way to turn it off for a fine placement. Premiere and Final Cut both switch snapping with S and show a magnet that says whether it is on.
notes: Found by measure-the-video-editor-against-premiere-and-fi (2026-09-24); gap report docs/design/video-vs-premiere.md. Reproduced: s with the timeline focused is taken by nobody (five-minute walk step 21). No toggle exists in Sources (grep 'snapping' in the timeline files only finds the key snap reach). Holding a modifier to suspend snapping while dragging is fine as well, if the walk shows it.
acceptance: S with the timeline focused switches snapping, and a magnet button in the timeline bar shows and switches the same state
With snapping off, a clip dragged near the playhead lands where it is let go
A walk switches snapping off, drags a clip to 0.1 s from the playhead and it lands there
